transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that I just don't seem to have the push I used to have. For things like choir, or my quilting, or... or even just visiting folks. 

Most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me to be out and about, but I just stay put.

Over the past couple of weeks, when you think about things you used to enjoy—like your choir or quilting—do you actually want to do them but just can't get yourself started, or is it more that they don't seem enjoyable to you anymore?

Well, like I was just saying, that push is just gone. I guess... I guess it's a bit of both. 

I think about going to choir or getting my quilting out, but I just don't have the want-to anymore. It just doesn't sound fun or bring me any joy right now. I know my friends are expecting me to show up, but I just can't get myself out of the chair to do it. It's just easier to sit there with the TV on.
How long have you been feeling this way—this lack of push and loss of enjoyment? Has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?
It's been longer than just a few weeks or months. I suppose... well, it's really been building up ever since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now.

Since you retired two years ago, have there been any periods—maybe weeks or months at a time—when you felt better, had more energy, and actually wanted to do things again? Or has it been pretty much this same way consistently throughout those two years?

No, I can't say that there have been. It's... well, it's been pretty much the exact same this whole time. I haven't really had any weeks or months where I suddenly got my energy back or wanted to go out and do things. It just sort of stays like this, day in and day out.

During these two years since you retired, have you had any days or weeks where your mood felt noticeably sadder or lower than this baseline you're describing—like times when you felt worse than you do right now?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had days where I felt a whole lot worse or sadder than this. It's just... well, it's just this same flat feeling all the time. I don't really dip down lower than how I am now.

Have you ever had a period—even just a few days—where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, had racing thoughts, or felt like you could do anything? A time when you were noticeably more talkative or active than your normal self?

No, I haven't ever had anything like that. I don't think I've ever felt unusually energetic or... or had racing thoughts. I sleep about the normal amount, I suppose. I'm not really an overly talkative person anyway, but there definitely haven't been any times where I felt like I could do anything. It's really just been this same tired, flat feeling I told you about.

Over these two years since retirement, have there been any weeks or even just a few days where your mood and energy felt closer to how they were before retirement—where things seemed a bit more enjoyable or you felt a bit more like yourself?

No, not really. I haven't had any days where I felt like my old self again. It's just... well, it's been pretty steady since I stopped working. I don't really find things enjoyable like I used to, not even for a few days. It just stays the same.

During these two years, have there been any times when you felt so low or depressed that it really interfered with your ability to take care of yourself—like trouble eating, sleeping much more or less than usual, or difficulty with personal hygiene?

No, nothing like that. I eat fine, I guess. I sleep okay. I still shower and get dressed every day. I just... I don't feel like doing much else, but I can still take care of myself. It's just that flat feeling, like I said. I haven't had any times where I couldn't manage the basics.

When you think back over these two years since retirement, has there been any time—even just a week or two—when you felt noticeably better than you do right now, with more energy and more interest in things?

No, I really haven't. Like I was saying, it's just been the same. I haven't had any weeks where I suddenly had more energy or wanted to do more. It's just been this... this same empty feeling the whole time since I retired. There hasn't been any break in it.
